title: THE ILLNESS EXPERIENCE OF WOMEN WITH INTERSTITIAL CYSTITIS (IC)/ BLADDER PAIN SYNDROME (BPS) – VIEW AND EXPERIENCE OF PATIENTS AND THEIR RELATIVES: A QUALITATIVE INVESTIGATION
summary:
Interstitial cystitis (IC)/bladder pain syndrome (BPS) is a chronic disease of the urinary bladder.
Typical symptoms of IC/BPS are:
- Persistent or recurrent chronic pain, pressure, or discomfort in the pelvic area that is perceived to be related to the urinary bladder
- At least one other symptom of urination, such as urinary urgency or frequent urination

IC/BPS can present with a wide range of symptoms that have a significant impact on quality of life and psychosocial well-being. Affected individuals and their families report negative impacts on life, such as social isolation, limited employment, anxiety, sleep disturbances, depressive symptoms, sexual dysfunction, and financial problems. 

To date, there is no consensus on the causes (etiology) or appropriate treatment of IC/BPS.

However, international guidelines emphasize the importance of self-management by affected individuals.

Little is known about the illness experience and the views and perceptions of women with IC/BPS. Similarly, little is known about the factors that facilitate the self-management of symptoms in everyday life and the barriers to doing so. 

This research project takes first steps to close these knowledge gaps.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Women of all ages, but at least 18 years old. The diagnosis of IC/BPS has been confirmed. Good ability to speak and understand the
German language. 

Relatives of women with IC/BPS of all ages,
but at least 18 years old. Good ability to speak and understand the German language.
Exclusion criteria:
Other pelvic floor dysfunctions that may additionally significantly influence the experience of the disease. These include pelvic organ prolapse (POP), urinary incontinence unrelated to IC/BPS, faecal incontinence, chronic pelvic pain unrelated to IC/BPS, sexual dysfunction unrelated to IC/BPS.
